q1: SELECT CUSTOMER_ID FROM CUSTOMER GROUP BY 1 HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT PRODUCT_KEY) = (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT PRODUCT_KEY) FROM PRODUCT)
q2: SELECT CUSTOMER_ID FROM CUSTOMER GROUP BY 1 HAVING GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT PRODUCT_KEY)=(SELECT GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT PRODUCT_KEY) FROM PRODUCT)
q1_prompt_sql: SELECT CUSTOMER_ID FROM CUSTOMER GROUP BY 1 HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT PRODUCT_KEY) = (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT PRODUCT_KEY) FROM PRODUCT)
q2_prompt_sql: SELECT CUSTOMER_ID FROM CUSTOMER GROUP BY 1 HAVING GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT PRODUCT_KEY)=(SELECT GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT PRODUCT_KEY) FROM PRODUCT)
explanation: Q1 and Q2 are not semantically equivalent. Q1 checks if the number of distinct product keys associated with each customer equals the total number of distinct product keys in the PRODUCT table. Q2 checks if the set of distinct product keys associated with each customer matches the set of all distinct product keys in the PRODUCT table exactly (not just the same count). This difference can lead to different results when a customer has the same count but not the same set of product keys.
counterexample_dsp: A scenario where one customer has a different set of product keys but the same count as the total number of products in the PRODUCT table.
